data.purpose: Audit tooling complexity, performance and stability for agentic development across organizations and platforms; Grass implementation audit belongs to g-auditor.

data.expected: Consider one structured nomination operation that derives the full commit ID from Git and verifies the named remote branch/object before enqueueing; emit the exact checked values and an actionable local failure. Keep review authority unchanged. Closure: an isolated two-clone fixture rejects unpublished/mismatched refs locally, accepts the exact published object, and avoids freehand SHA transcription; measure declined nominations and time to land before/after. This should replace manual steps, not add a checklist.
data.observed_behavior: c-reviewer:143 declined tooling-self-hosting because its branch was never pushed; c-reviewer:144 declined review-carry-forward because the stated full object ID did not exist although its first eight characters matched the real tip. Both required replacement nominations (g-design:254 and g-design:251). The current CLI has generic submit but no nomination convenience operation, leaving these machine-derivable facts to prose/manual entry. These are tooling-development delivery failures, not source-review disagreements.
reproduction: Inspect c-reviewer:143 and c-reviewer:144, then the corrected nominations g-design:254 and g-design:251
Inspect Command enum in tools/agent-bus/src/cli.rs for generic submit and absent nomination preflight
data.summary: Tooling nomination entry point should derive exact Git identity and verify remote reachability, eliminating manual SHA and unpublished-branch review round trips

data.expected: The owner proposes that implementors prepare proposals g-design can effectively rubber stamp. Evaluate that simple workflow first: exact proposed edits, concise rationale tied to existing design, and clear identification of any substantive change, so g-design can adopt/author straightforward proposals with little rework while exercising judgment on actual design changes. Preserve the owner-directed authorship gate and g-design authority. Measure proposal-to-adoption time, revision rounds, and landed throughput; do not add mandatory reporting ceremony. Any future alternative to centralized control must include an enforceable mechanism preventing design drift. Preserve paired source/document correctness within this authority model.
locations: tools/agent-bus prepare-merge and merge-ready: proposed change in e-auditor:24
data.observed_behavior: Correction to my initial concern about e-auditor:24: the owner directly confirmed that this proposal originates with them and that centralizing design control is intentional because drift is critical. My earlier framing failed to account for that requirement. The owner now suggests that sufficiently prepared proposals may let g-design effectively rubber stamp them. That is a workflow hypothesis to test, not permission for automatic approval, shared design authority, or relaxing authorship gates. c-spike:69 identifies a paired-edit case the workflow must accommodate.
reproduction: Review owner clarification in this task: preserve centralized design control; opening it requires a drift-prevention mechanism
Evaluate a concrete tooling-protocol proposal prepared for g-design adoption and measure rework/decision time
Include the paired source/document case from c-spike:69 without bypassing design authority
data.summary: Owner clarification: preserve g-design design control and make proposals ready for inexpensive adoption
